prompts.text: Name a job Bill Gates would mark "Human Reserved."
notes: Reading flags are guesses: check which jobs Gates actually names. Baseball comes from his line that we won't want to watch computers play baseball; biologist, programmer and energy expert from the professions he's said will last.
The list is human-centred jobs only. Clearly automatable jobs (cashier, data entry clerk, bookkeeper, telemarketer) bounce on purpose.

prompts.text: Name a life event you'd want to hear about from a human.

a death in the family: the death of a loved one
infertility: not being able to have kids

list: a parent going into a care home
notes: Generic aliases point at the common answers; the Human Reserved answers only take close paraphrases, so 'rejection' on its own is First-Hand Thinker and 'a rejection letter' is Human Reserved.

prompts.text: Name something governments could tax if robots take the jobs.
prompts.source: Gates, "The Turbulent AI Era"; Bastani, Fully Automated Luxury Communism
notes: Reading flags: Gates's robot tax and the token tax from the theory map. Robots is also the AI's sealed answer, so the reading answer lands on Meat Proxy, which is the point.
'Income' and 'sales' are on the list because they are correct, even though they shrink when the jobs go.

prompts.text: Name something work gives you besides a paycheque.
prompts.source: Gordon and Gunkel, "AI and the Future of Work"

a reason to get dressed: a reason to get dressed in the morning
a reason to put on pants

list: a reason to leave the house
notes: Reading flags follow the four goods of work Gordon and Gunkel draw on (excellence, social contribution, community, recognition). Check the wording against the reading.
Community is both a reading answer and a common AI answer, so it lands on Prompt Zombie with the 📚 badge.

prompts.text: Name a public service that should be free for everyone.
notes: Reading flags: Bastani's universal basic services (healthcare, education, transport, housing, information). Check against the reading. Healthcare is the AI's sealed answer, so the reading answer scores 0 with the 📚 badge.

prompts.text: Name a hobby you'd keep if robots did all the work.
prompts.source: Sweet, "Is Fully Automated Luxury Communism Desirable?"; Gordon and Gunkel
notes: Hobby lists are wide on purpose: almost any real hobby is correct, so creative answers rarely bounce.

prompts.text: Name a job machines already took from humans.
notes: Reading flag: aircraft spotting, the Ground Observer Corps job SAGE automated (Packer and Reeves). 'Computer' on its own counts as Human Reserved because the first computers were people.
'Horse' is accepted for the peak-horse argument even though it isn't a human job: the reading makes the analogy explicit.
Some list entries were only partly automated (chess player, translator, warehouse worker). Keep or cut them after the runs.
